I am getting older, so on 5 mu I am not going to do anything fancy. I will still keep the wheat-maize rotation on the same land because that is the safest way for me. Wheat and maize are what I know, and with only 5 mu I care more about steady grain and not losing money than chasing some big yield target. I have farmed this land for many years. If I cut fertilizer too much, yield usually suffers, but if I push too hard, then cash goes out and irrigation and fertilizer both cost money. So this year I will stay close to the usual local practice, with a moderate fertilizer rate and a few key irrigations from the well. My family can still help some, but since some people work off-farm, I will arrange the main jobs at the important times and hire a little help or machine service if the wheat harvest and maize sowing are too tight together.

For wheat, I will sow in early October with a common improved variety that people around here use, not the most expensive seed. I will put base fertilizer before sowing, then topdress once around jointing depending on how the crop looks. I will irrigate at the key stages, mainly before winter if the soil is dry, at jointing, and at grain filling if needed. For maize, I will plant right after wheat harvest in mid-June because that planting window is short. I will use hybrid seed, put part of the fertilizer at sowing, then topdress once at the big flare stage. If summer rain is decent, I may only irrigate once, but if it turns dry I will do two times. I do not spray pesticides on a fixed schedule; I spray when I see weeds or insects becoming a real problem. That way I keep cost under control.
